name: ThreeSum1960614_Machine_Bundle008
definition_title: Compiler contracts, reusable tasks, and trimmed block encodings
natural_language_statement:
For a finite Light program $P$, a verdict mode $\delta$, and a Light step count $c$, the compiled step budget is the affine function

$$T_{P,\delta}(c)=\operatorname{startCost}(P,\delta)+\operatorname{stepsPerStep}(\operatorname{dispPos}(P,\delta))c.$$

Stack-space and negative-address bounds depend on the program text and the allowed call depth. The compiler input contract represents the Light memory in word-RAM cells and puts two bounded integer arguments into designated cells. Its outcome contract represents the final memory and result, preserves the argument cells, and preserves cells beyond the allowed positive and negative working regions. The bundle also defines segment-copy, constant-fill, and entrywise linear-combination programs and the associated program-proof tactic interface.

A procedure need consists of a word bound, extra cell count, and extra call depth. For a free pointer $f$ and current depth $d$, it is admissible when these requirements fit the run limits, including $f+\mathrm{cells}\le\mathrm{space}$ and $d+\mathrm{depth}\le\mathrm{maxDepth}$. Polynomial need bounds have the form $2^s((n+1)(U+1))^k$, for fixed natural exponents $s,k$. A task-solving specification requires the procedure contract to hold in every extension of its finite program, for every permitted input, memory, bound, and free pointer; its real-valued runtime form also bounds the natural execution budget uniformly for $n,U\ge1$ and every real upper bound $u\ge U$.

For each input size $n$, the executable band size is $B=\lceil R/D\rceil$, where $R$ is the integer ceiling of the square root of the typed output count and $D=2^{\lfloor62656016\mu(n)/1000000000\rfloor}$. The included rounding facts give $0<B$ and $R\le DB<R+D$. Block endpoint encodings flatten $J$ local subsets of $464h$ coordinates. Left and right admissibility independently require exactly $h$ coordinates per block and a hash bucket within its cap. Disjoint admissible endpoints reconstruct retained choice tuples. Their natural-number histograms count indices in finite sets whose integer residues match the positional endpoint encoding, with an additional offset on the right.

These contracts connect reusable imperative procedures, exact rounded parameters, and independently trimmed combinatorial histograms in the deterministic integer 3SUM runtime proof. The compiler and routine interfaces retain the pinned upstream attribution.

name: ThreeSum1960614_Machine_Bundle009
definition_title: Arithmetic routines and Light-to-word-RAM solver specifications
natural_language_statement:
This bundle defines finite Light programs for Euclidean remainder, rounded logarithms, rounded cube root, rounded halving, merging, power tables, and integer square root. For an integer $x$ and positive modulus $M$, the remainder program uses a doubling table and sign correction; its precondition reserves logarithmically many cells and a word bound at least $4V+4M+16$ for inputs bounded by $V$. The local-only routines target $\lfloor\log_2x\rfloor$ (zero at $x=0$), $\lceil\log_2x\rceil$ (zero for $x\le1$), $\lceil\sqrt[3]{x}\rceil$, $\lceil x/2\rceil$, and $\lfloor\sqrt{x}\rfloor$. Merge copies the recursively defined merge of two integer lists into a disjoint output segment; its invariant records consumed prefixes, the output length, and preservation outside that segment. Power-table invariants record the entries $1,b,\ldots,b^{j-1}$ and current power $b^j$.

For a word-RAM problem, a Light program specification quantifies over every input in the stated domain and requires a correct terminating execution within its real time bound. Run limits are polynomially bounded in the input parameters. A two-stage matrix specification additionally bounds preprocessing time, space and call depth, establishes a memory predicate, and requires every subsequent query to return the requested matrix-product entry while preserving that predicate. The bundle defines the program-dependent word-size slope and time constant used when transferring these specifications to the target word RAM. Its 3SUM task takes $N,U\ge1$, a length-$N$ integer list bounded by $U$, and a memory segment below the free pointer; the specified result indicates whether three distinct positions sum to zero.

For a global output $q$, a set $I$ of completed blocks, and fixed left subsets $u_i$, completed choice tuples have output $q$ and those fixed left endpoints on $I$. Residual subsets lie in the remaining output coordinates and must reconstruct independently admissible left and right endpoints. With finite index sets $B,C$, integer label maps $b,c$, and integer modulus/offset parameters $P,d$, the stored prefix value is a signed subset-Moebius query of the product of the two partial zeta transforms, evaluated over the residual output set.

These definitions expose the executable arithmetic, machine-transfer contracts, and forced-prefix query meaning needed to prove the full deterministic integer 3SUM runtime bound. The underlying language-library routines retain the pinned upstream attribution.
